lesson.grammar_point: past forms for polite distance (I was hoping we could / I wanted to check / we were thinking of + -ing)

listenings.text: Hi Andreia, it's Brian. You asked me for some tips before your first call with the Boston team, so here they are. First, be punctual. In the United States, a call at nine means nine, not nine ten. Second, keep the small talk short. Two minutes is fine, and then people want to get to the point. That is not rude, it is just a different style. Third, Americans are quite straightforward, but they are rarely blunt. They say things like I wanted to check or I was hoping we could, and that soft tone is important. Finally, your Latin American colleagues usually need more time to build rapport. So, as the person in the middle, give a little space to both styles. You will be great.

Hi everyone, and thank you for joining from three different time zones. I know it's early in Mexico City, so thank you, Lucia. I was hoping we could keep this call to forty minutes. First, I wanted to check that everyone can hear me well. If you're not speaking, please stay on mute, and unmute when you have a question. Today we have two points: the training calendar for the new nurses and the simulator schedule. We were thinking of starting the training in March, but we are open to other dates. Tom, could we start with you? And Lucia, I would love to hear your view after that. Let's touch base again next week.
